## Try It Yourself

::: {.callout-tip}
## How to Practice
1. **Run the code** to build your first regression model
2. **Read the output** carefully — each number tells you something
3. **Copy to RStudio** for your notebook exercises
:::

### Fit a Simple Regression Model

```{webr-r}
# Predict wellbeing from stress
model <- lm(wellbeing ~ stress, data = wellbeing)
summary(model)
```

::: {.callout-note}
## Key Output
- **Coefficients**: Intercept (b₀) and slope for stress (b₁)
- **R-squared**: Proportion of variance explained
- **F-statistic**: Overall model significance
:::

### Extract the Equation

```{webr-r}
model <- lm(wellbeing ~ stress, data = wellbeing)
b0 <- round(coef(model)[1], 2)
b1 <- round(coef(model)[2], 2)

cat("Regression equation:\n")
cat("Wellbeing =", b0, "+", b1, "× Stress\n\n")
cat("The slope of", b1, "means: for every 1-point increase in stress,\n")
cat("wellbeing changes by", b1, "points.")
```

### Make Predictions

```{webr-r}
model <- lm(wellbeing ~ stress, data = wellbeing)

# Predict for three stress values
new_data <- data.frame(stress = c(10, 25, 40))
predictions <- predict(model, new_data)

for (i in 1:3) {
  cat("Stress =", new_data$stress[i], "→ Predicted wellbeing =",
      round(predictions[i], 1), "\n")
}
```

### Visualise the Model

```{webr-r}
model <- lm(wellbeing ~ stress, data = wellbeing)

plot(wellbeing$stress, wellbeing$wellbeing,
     main = "Simple Regression: Wellbeing ~ Stress",
     xlab = "Stress", ylab = "Wellbeing",
     pch = 19, col = "steelblue")
abline(model, col = "red", lwd = 2)
```
